tagline: Where East meets West — domes, minarets, golden light over the Bosphorus.
bestSeason: Apr–May / Sep–Oct (mild, fewer crowds, soft light)

spots.name: Hagia Sophia
spots.bestTime: Early morning (08:00–09:00) before the tour buses arrive
angles: Shoot the exterior from Sultanahmet Square to the northwest — the four minarets frame the central dome symmetrically.
Inside, point straight up at the central dome and use the lower thirds for the hanging calligraphy medallions. Brace on a railing — it's dim, so you'll be around 1/30s.
For scale, place a person in the lower frame against the massive arches — it tells the story of the building's size.
spots.gear: Wide 16mm (24mm equiv) or wider for interiors. Bump ISO to 3200–6400; the interior is darker than it looks.

spots.name: Blue Mosque
spots.bestTime: Blue hour (just after sunset) when the mosque is lit and the sky is deep blue
angles: Best vantage is from the gardens between Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia — the fountain gives you a foreground and leading line to the domes.
Get low and shoot the cascading domes (the 'wedding cake' stack) slightly off-centre for depth rather than dead-on symmetry.
Inside, shoot upward into the dome to capture the famous İznik blue tiles — the colour is why Velvia's saturation works beautifully here.
spots.gear: Tripod for blue hour (exposures of 1–4s). Polarising filter cuts glare on the tiles.

spots.name: Galata Tower
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon into sunset — climb the tower ~1 hour before golden hour
angles: Shoot the tower itself from the narrow cobbled streets of Galata looking up — the converging buildings act as a natural frame.
From the top, the best panorama is southeast over the Golden Horn toward the old city skyline. Wait for the call to prayer at sunset for atmosphere.
Catch the seagulls — they circle the tower constantly. Pre-focus and shoot bursts to get a bird in frame with the dome behind.
spots.gear: 35mm (50mm equiv) for street compression below; wide for the rooftop panorama. Tower gets crowded — go at opening.

spots.name: Grand Bazaar
spots.bestTime: Mid-morning (10:00–12:00) — shops open, light streams through skylights
angles: Use the painted vaulted ceilings as a leading line — stand in the middle of an aisle and let the arches recede into the distance.
Shoot the lamp shops: hundreds of hanging mosaic lanterns. Expose for the lit lamps and let the surroundings fall darker for drama.
Candid stall portraits work well — ask first, then shoot the merchant amid their colourful goods. Fujicolor 200's punchy colour suits the spices and textiles.
spots.gear: Fast prime (f/2 or wider) for the dim interior. Keep ISO flexible 1600–6400. Watch your bag — it's crowded.

spots.name: Bosphorus & Maiden's Tower
spots.nameZh: 博斯普魯斯海峽與少女塔
spots.bestTime: Golden hour from a Bosphorus ferry, or sunrise from Üsküdar shore
angles: From the public ferry (Eminönü–Üsküdar), shoot the old-city skyline with the mosques silhouetted against the setting sun. Stand on the upper deck, stern side.
Maiden's Tower sits mid-strait — frame it with a passing ferry or fishing boat for scale and a sense of movement.
At the Galata Bridge, the fishermen's rods make a great repeating foreground element pointing toward the skyline.
spots.gear: Telephoto 50–200mm (75–300 equiv) to compress the skyline from the water. Eterna's muted tones suit hazy, backlit harbour light.
